content.text:
Let me analyze. Kingswood has footman 25 and knight 26, with March +1. Reachable: storms-end (ours, no gain), the-boneway (neutral, no castle), the-reach (castle, capture gains one castle area without combat).

The Reach is empty (controller null, no units, no neutral force). Marching there gains a castle area. Let's check: the-reach has castle=1. Moving units there captures it.

But wait, we could also split - move one unit to the-reach and keep one in Kingswood to preserve control. Kingswood has no power token (controlPowerToken null), so if we vacate all, we lose it unless we leave a token.

Actually best: capture The Reach (gains 1 castle area) while keeping Kingswood. We could move just enough to capture. The Reach is empty, so any single unit takes it. Move footman 25 to the-reach, keep knight 26 in Kingswood (preserves control, no power token needed).

Wait but do we need to worry about The Reach being attacked? The Reach is adjacent to many things: blackwater, dornish-marches, highgarden, kings-landing, kingswood, searoad-marches, the-boneway. Tyrell has dornish-marches with support order and 3 units there. Lannister in blackwater? Let's see blackwater not listed with units. Tyrell dornish-marches support +0 adjacent to the-reach, could support an attack against us.

But this move doesn't require combat; The Reach is empty. We just move in. Later opponents could attack. That's fine.

Actually, should we move both units to The Reach to make it defensible, leaving Kingswood with a power token? Kingswood contributes 0 castle. The Reach gives +1 castle. Losing Kingswood would drop our land areas but no castle.

Let's think about victory: we have 3 castle areas currently (sunspear stronghold, yronwood castle, storms-end castle). Capturing The Reach gives 4 castle areas. That's good progress.

If we move both units to The Reach, Kingswood becomes empty. We could leave a power token (costs 1 of our 3 power). Kingswood has no castle, but it's a land area with supply 1 and crown 1. Losing it loses 1 land area and a crown icon. Not huge but we'd want it.

Option A: Move footman 25 to the-reach, leave knight 26 in Kingswood. Result: The Reach captured (1 unit), Kingswood still controlled (knight). No power spent. Clean.

But a single footman in The Reach is vulnerable. Does that matter? Tyrell might attack. But we want the castle area now.

Actually wait - do we get castle credit immediately? Yes, controlling area with unit.

Option B: Move both to The Reach, leave power token in Kingswood. Then The Reach has knight+footman (army of 2). Kingswood controlled via token. Costs 1 power. This is stronger defensively at The Reach and keeps Kingswood. But army of 2 at The Reach, and one footman at Sunspear, one at Storms-end, one at Yronwood - all singles. Supply 2 means: armies sizes permitted for supply 2: 3,2,2. We'd have one army of 2 (fine). Good.

Option C: Move both to the-reach, no token, lose Kingswood.

I think Option B is best: capture The Reach with a full army and keep Kingswood via power token (we can afford 1 of 3 power). This maximizes castles while preserving land.

Hmm, but let me consider whether keeping both units at Kingswood vs The Reach matters for future. Actually The Reach being adjacent to Tyrell's dornish-marches (3 units + support) means we might get attacked. Having 2 units there (knight+footman = str 3) plus we'd defend... but our defense would need order next round.

Actually, do we have any orders on The Reach? No. So if Tyrell attacks, we defend with raw strength.

Alternatively, keep both at Kingswood and don't expand? No, capturing a castle is valuable.

Let me reconsider: is there risk in vacating Kingswood? If we move both out and leave token, we keep control. Fine.

But there's another consideration: Could we capture The Reach AND also send a unit to the-boneway? No, only one destination may... actually the-boneway is empty (controller null) too. But no castle there. Splitting to two non-combat destinations is allowed (only combat limited to one). But the-boneway gives nothing except land. Not worth losing the castle region.

Let me go with Option B: both units (25,26) to the-reach, leave_power_token true.

Wait—leaving a power token costs 1 power, we have 3. Fine.

Hmm, but actually consider: if we leave Kingswood with just a power token and no units, an enemy can take it by moving in. But that's true regardless.

Alternatively Option A leaves a knight in Kingswood which defends it. Which is better? The Reach with 1 footman could be retaken easily. Kingswood with a knight is decent.

Let me think about what threatens. Tyrell at dornish-marches (footman, footman, knight = 4 str) adjacent to the-reach. If Tyrell marches into The Reach, they'd need to beat our defender. With a single footman we lose easily. With knight+footman we have 3 and could maybe hold with support. But Tyrell has a support order at dornish-marches (support +0) which is adjacent to The Reach and could support themselves... wait can a support order in the same area as the marching army support? Support comes from adjacent areas to the battlefield. dornish-marches is adjacent to the-reach, and Tyrell marches from dornish-marches... Actually the support order at dornish-marches: if Tyrell marches FROM dornish-marches, the units leave, but the support order? Support order is on dornish-marches area. If the area is vacated... hmm. Actually the support order at dornish-marches would be the marching order region if they use it to march. But they placed Support +0 there. So Tyrell isn't marching from there this round with that order. They can't both support and march from same area.

So Tyrell's dornish-marches is a support order, not a march. So Tyrell isn't attacking The Reach from there this round. Good.

Other adjacent to the-reach: blackwater, kings-landing (Lannister? no, neutral garrison 5), searoad-marches, kingswood, the-boneway, highgarden (Tyrell march +0 with 2 footmen), dornish-marches.

Highgarden has March +0. Tyrell could march from highgarden to the-reach. Highgarden has 2 footmen. That would be an attack of 2 vs our defense. If we have knight+footman (3), we win. If just footman (1), we lose.

So moving both to The Reach is safer. But then Kingswood left via token.

Hmm, actually since it's our turn now and Tyrell acts later, they could respond. But we can't fully control that.

Actually wait, an important point: The Reach is currently unoccupied. If we march both units there, we control it. But next round Tyrell could attack. For now, we get the castle.

Let me consider a middle ground: move knight 26 to the-reach, leave footman 25 in Kingswood. Then The Reach has knight (str 2), Kingswood has footman. No power spent. The Reach defends with 2 + possible support. Hmm, but Highgarden's 2 footmen could tie/beat.

Actually knight+footman = 3 is better. I'll go with moving both, leaving power token.

Hmm, wait, but there's a subtlety: do we want to keep a unit in Kingswood to later march it? Kingswood currently is our staging area. It borders the-reach, storms-end, the-boneway, and via... Actually kingswood is adjacent to blackwater-bay, kings-landing, shipbreaker-bay, storms-end, the-boneway, the-reach. 

If we leave Kingswood empty with token, we still control it but no units.

I think taking The Reach strongly is good. Let me decide: move 25 and 26 to the-reach, leave power token true.

Actually, let me reconsider whether leaving power token is worth it. We have 3 power. Power is used for bidding (Clash of Kings) and wildlings. Spending 1 loses value. Kingswood gives 0 castle but 1 supply icon and 1 crown icon. Losing it costs a land area and icons. Since we're not at risk of supply crunch... Holding Kingswood is nice. 1 power is cheap. I'll leave the token.

Hmm, but actually is Kingswood's control even important? It contributes to "controlled land areas" tiebreaker. We have 5 land areas. Keeping it helps. Also the supply icon matters for supply card. Let me just leave it.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider: might it be better to keep a unit in Kingswood (footman) and move only the knight to The Reach, avoiding the power cost, and having a defender in Kingswood? Then The Reach has a knight only.

Trade-offs:
- Option B (both to Reach, token in Kingswood): The Reach defended by 3; Kingswood controlled but undefended (token only). Cost 1 power.
- Option A (footman to Reach, knight in Kingswood): The Reach defended by 1; Kingswood defended by 2. No power.

If Tyrell attacks The Reach from Highgarden with 2 footmen (+0 march): Option B: we defend 3 > 2, win, keep castle. Option A: we defend 1 < 2, lose castle and unit.

So Option B protects the newly gained castle. That's key since we want to keep castle areas. I'll go Option B.

But wait, in Option B, if enemy takes Kingswood, we lose a land area but keep the castle. Better.

However, one concern: if we leave Kingswood with only a power token and no units, is that legal/does it preserve control? Yes—establishing control when vacating with a March order.

Can we leave a power token? canLeavePowerToken: true. We have 3 power. Good.

Also supply: The Reach army = knight + footman = 2 units, one army of size 2. Supply 2 permits 3,2,2. Fine. Other areas: sunspear footman(1), storms-end footman(35), yronwood footman(27), sea-of-dorne ship(24), salt-shore token. All singles except... port-of-sunspear, port-of-storms-end. All singles. Good.

Wait, actually I should double check "the-reach" capture gains one castle area "without combat". Yes empty.

Let me also consider: could we instead send units to the-boneway to expand? Not castle. Not needed.

Decision: moves [{destination_region_id: "the-reach", unit_ids:[25,26]}], leave_power_token: true.

Hmm, but let me reconsider one more time. Is there value in keeping knight in Kingswood? The Reach is a castle=1 (single castle area). We really want to secure it. Moving both is best.

Actually, hold on. Let me reconsider whether attacking would be better. No enemies reachable from kingswood except none. Storms-end ours, the-boneway empty, the-reach empty. So no combat.

I'm fairly confident. Let me quickly verify The Reach is empty via check_neighbours? The observation already shows it's not in board list... Actually the board list doesn't include the-reach entry. It's not listed among controlled regions, so it's neutral/empty. The actionGuidance says controller null, no neutral force, no combat. Good.

Let me just submit. Actually I'll do a quick check_neighbours on the-reach to confirm support/defense situation, but it's not necessary since no combat. I'll skip to save time... but instructions suggest verifying. It's empty, no combat, so not needed.

I'll submit final.

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.
moves.title: Moves

leave_power_token.description: Spend one available power token to preserve control when legally vacating the source area. This must be false if units remain or control cannot be established.
leave_power_token.title: Leave Power Token

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Before attacking another army, use check_neighbours on that battlefield to verify the supporting areas. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
